question: Which maintained open-source MuJoCo robot model is suitable for FDB v2 fixed-arm manipulation?
search_queries: MuJoCo Menagerie Franka Panda license actuators gripper

sources.title: MuJoCo Menagerie
claims: Menagerie curates MuJoCo robot models and reports per-model licenses.
The package pins model releases and exposes model object IDs for provenance.

sources.title: Franka Emika Panda MJCF description
claims: The model is Apache-2.0 and derived from the public Panda URDF.
It provides seven arm position actuators, finger mimic constraint, gripper tendon, and gripper actuator.

cross_checks: The installed 2026.9.0 registry reports Apache-2.0 and object ID 3d2262eeb81ecec19abfa31dd509e35abbb33e67.
The compiled model exposes 9 joints and 8 actuators; limits were read from mjModel rather than copied from prose.
interpretation: Panda provides a maintained, licensed arm-plus-gripper baseline. FDB should load the pinned Menagerie artifact and derive morphology directly from the compiled model.
hypotheses: MuJoCo body Jacobians plus joint-limit-clamped DLS can establish a reach baseline without custom kinematics.
A single-target reach result is insufficient to validate generalized reach.

validation.protocol: Inspect compiled morphology, solve three DLS damping candidates, execute with model position actuators, and measure Cartesian error and joint limits.
validation.result: All candidates converged; selected execution error was 0.00529 m with no limit violations or contacts.

unresolved_questions: How well does reach generalize across workspace targets and orientation constraints?
How should collision-free reach candidates be generated?
